headline: Grade-configuration task force recommends three follow-up steps, including a feasibility study of one comprehensive middle school.
summary: The task force presentation projected about 660 students at Andrews Middle School in school year 28-29 if all of grades 7 and 8 attend there, and said the building was designed for about 600. Its three recommendations are an advisory committee review of middle school models, reporting back in April 2027; a feasibility study of one comprehensive middle school with stakeholder surveys; and a look at redistricting. Also tabled were the 2027-28 district calendar and an elementary school reassignment policy, and a report on a delayed school opening was approved, with the report requested for January.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda: bills and payrolls, budget transfers, journal entry 21307 for $613,041, and meeting minutes.
Tabled the 2027-28 district calendar until the next meeting.
Approved support for the grade configuration task force's recommendations.
Tabled the elementary school reassignment policy.
Approved, as amended, a feasibility report on delayed school opening.
discussion: Grade configuration task force: The task force found that Andrews Middle School cannot hold two full grade spans. Members said the choice comes down to what the buildings can house and to facilities.

Redistricting: One member proposed drafting a policy for automatic redistricting every certain number of years, with a draft for the next meeting. Others said that redistricting is hard on families and that small boundary changes should be considered first.
Elementary reassignment policy: Members asked whether the mutual benefit test for sibling requests was clear to families. They also asked whether the sibling item should be removed or reworded.

2027-28 school calendar: Members asked to move a professional development day to June and to cut testing in May. The superintendent said June could be brought back, but May is tricky because of MCAS and MAP testing.

English learner progress results: The presentation said 76% of elementary English learners met progress targets, an increase of more than 22 percentage points. Secondary results fell, to 33% in grades 6 through 8 and 25% at the high school.
